This is the one place in the package that quotes benchmark numbers. They come
from two studies in the research repository: the simplification study of
2026-09-28/29, which chose the engines (`research/simplify/`: `FINDINGS.md`,
and the report *Simplifying spiDE* on the
[research site](https://bhuvalab.github.io/spiDE-research/)), and the depth
benchmark of 2026-09-30, which chose how sequencing depth enters
(`research/bench2/`: the pre-registration and its dated log in
`BENCHMARK.md`, the tables in `tables/`). When a default changes on new
evidence, this vignette changes with it.

# What "calibrated" means here

A spiDE test is calibrated if, on data where the hypothesis it tests is true
by construction, its $z$ statistics have unit spread in every expression band
and a Benjamini-Hochberg screen at 0.05 rarely makes any call. Two nulls,
both built from real cohorts:

- **the block null** (the niche is shuffled): each section's niche field is
  shifted toroidally by a random offset, and every cell takes the niche
  densities found at its shifted position. This destroys the association
  between a cell's niche and its expression while keeping the niche field's
  spatial smoothness. Every niche slope is zero, so both tests
  are null.
- **the permutation null** (the condition is shuffled): the condition label
  is permuted across patients within slide, so a slide effect cannot pass for
  a condition effect. The niche slopes are the real ones, so only the
  condition-specific test, and the filtered procedure, are null.

The pass criteria, fixed before the validation nulls were scored:

| reading | criterion |
|---|---|
| per-band spread: median RMS of null $z$ in each quintile of expression, per index type | in [0.90, 1.10], for the condition test on both nulls and the pooled test on the block null |
| tail, block null: fraction of null grids with at least one BH call at 0.05 | at most 0.10, both tests |
| tail, permutation null: fraction of permutations with at least one BH call at 0.05 | at most 0.07, condition test over every triplet and over the filtered family |

# The cohorts

Five comparisons in four cohorts, each at the bandwidth of its earlier runs,
restricted to the five best-covered index types:

| cohort | platform, tissue | condition | patients | bandwidth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GSE250346 | Xenium, lung (pulmonary fibrosis) | control 9, disease 26 | 35 | 60 µm |
| GSE282639 | CosMx 1k, lung (IPF) | control 13, IPF 15 | 28 | 30 µm |
| GSE289194 | CosMx 1k, lymph node | extranodal 20, nodal 24 | 44 | 30 µm |
| YTMA | CosMx WTA, NSCLC | non-responder 30, responder 25 | 55 | 30 µm |
| YTMA stage | CosMx WTA, LUAD | early 123, late 40 | 163 | 30 µm |

**The three public cohorts carry the decisions.** The YTMA data are under
review for suspected data issues (a decision of 2026-09-29), and enter only
as a sensitivity analysis at a quarter of a public cohort's weight.

# Results

## The slopes engine (the default)

With its effective-patient df and expression-trended prior, on fresh
validation nulls (ten block grids and 1,000 permutations per cohort, never
used in its development), the slopes engine passes every criterion in all
five comparisons:

- per-band null RMS 0.909-0.984;
- worst permutation tail 0.034;
- worst block tail 0.10 (GSE250346, pooled test), at the limit.

Without the effective-patient df the pooled test's block tail reached 0.40
(the weights can rest on a few cell-rich patients when the between-patient
variance truncates to zero); without the trend, bright genes' spread was
tilted. Both fixes were required by public cohorts, not only by YTMA.

## The sandwich engine

On 160 null grids across the five comparisons, the per-band null RMS lies in
0.94-1.10 and the condition-specific test over every triplet made no false
call. Its filtered procedure made a false call in 9 of 100 permutations on
GSE289194 (95% interval roughly 0.04-0.16, against the 0.07 limit), its one
miss.

## The mixed model of spiDE 0.99.22

On every cohort and both nulls, every grid produced false calls (21 to 3,593
per grid on average), with per-band null RMS as high as 5.95. Its standard errors
had no between-patient variance in the niche slopes. Replacing only its
standard errors (patient-clustered sandwiches with an effective df) moved it
most of the way but left 5-25% excess spread. It is archived as the research
package `spiDEmixed`.

# Power

Paired plasmode on the public cohorts: effects of 0.25 and 0.5 SD of the
niche covariate planted into real counts by binomial thinning, shared by all
patients or varying between them; true-positive rate at BH 0.05, averaged
over both tests and both kinds of effect.

| | slopes engine | sandwich engine |
|---|---|---|
| true-positive rate, public cohorts | 0.679 | 0.499 |
| effects varying between patients | 0.589 | 0.283 |
| effects shared by all patients | 0.768 | 0.715 |
| realised false discovery proportion | 0.023 | 0.048 |
| GSE250346 / GSE289194 / GSE282639 | 0.853 / 0.719 / 0.464 | 0.577 / 0.494 / 0.425 |

On the two YTMA comparisons the order reverses (0.089 against 0.140, and
0.253 against 0.365): in sparse whole-transcriptome data, with effects shared
by all patients, the effective-patient df costs the slopes engine the most.
With YTMA at a quarter weight the slopes engine still leads (0.61 against
0.46). Across all five comparisons the effective-patient df costs about 0.03
in true-positive rate (0.476 against 0.508 without it), which is the price of
the calibration above.

**The default is the slopes engine** because it passes every null and is the
more powerful where it matters most, on effects that vary between patients.
Use the sandwich engine when effects are expected to be shared by all
patients, or as a check.

# Depth: why `depth = "loglib"` is the default

Library size in spatial data mixes technical capture with biological RNA
content, and the content can depend on the niche. So depth handling was
judged **against the estimand**, not by how little library-size association
the residuals keep: removing all of it would also remove biology.

**The benchmark.** A simulator fitted to real cohorts (real positions, cell
types, patients and niche densities; a gene-specific, spatially varying
library-size response taken from per-section SpaNorm fits) generated counts
under six depth scenarios: independent depth, smooth technical depth,
technical depth aligned with a niche, niche-driven RNA content, both of the
last two together, and a doubled gene-specific response. Effects on the
condition contrast were planted, shared by all patients or varying between
them. Two estimands were scored: **technical depth removed** (the planted
effect plus any niche-driven content) and **relative** (the planted effect
alone). The decision rule was registered before any run.

**Which templates count.** Only templates whose simulations passed a
pre-registered realism gate carry the decision: GSE289194 (weight 1) and YTMA
(weight 0.25, its data being under review). GSE282639 and GSE250346 failed
the gate on the per-gene depth slope and are reported without weight.

**Calibration.** Every depth option passed on GSE289194 in every scenario:
per-band null RMS of `z` 0.93-1.00, permutation tails at most 0.015, and no
false call on any of the 12 block-shifted grids per scenario. (YTMA: bands
0.95-1.01, tails at most 0.024.)

**Accuracy.** The worst scenario's relative bias of the condition contrast,
technical-depth-removed estimand:

| `depth` | GSE289194 | YTMA |
|---|---|---|
| spatial library-size spline | -0.130 | -0.221 |
| `loglib` | -0.135 | -0.225 |
| `nonlinear` | -0.135 | -0.226 |
| SpaNorm library-size offset | -0.145 | -0.233 |

Weighted, the options lie within 0.015 of each other, inside the
pre-registered tie margin of 0.02, and the tie goes to the simplest:
`"loglib"`. Power is the same for all of them (filtered-family true-positive
rate 0.816-0.819 on GSE289194). The spatial spline is kept as an option: it
costs 1.2-1.55 times the `"loglib"` fit.

**Two findings to know when reading results.**

- **Niche-driven RNA content is removed with depth.** When the niche raises a
  cell's total RNA, every option that adjusts for observed library size also
  removes that content from the pooled niche slope (relative bias about -0.7
  against the technical-depth-removed estimand, in every depth option). A
  pooled slope therefore reports expression relative to the cell's total
  RNA. The condition contrast is affected only through content that differs
  between conditions.
- **The slopes engine understates the condition contrast**: by 10-14% on
  GSE289194 and about 22% on YTMA, under both estimands, where the sandwich
  engine is within 5%. Its tests stay calibrated and it keeps more than twice
  the sandwich engine's power (true-positive rate 0.82 against 0.34 on
  GSE289194), so the default is unchanged, but read its estimates as
  conservative in size. The cause is being investigated (it is not the
  one-step approximation of the per-patient slope).
- **The sandwich engine's null spread ran wide on GSE289194**: up to 1.13 in
  one expression band, outside the 0.90-1.10 limit, where every slopes-engine
  option stayed inside it.

# Not yet measured
- **Gene sets.** `spiGSEA()` has not been through a gene-set null and is
  experimental.
- **Bandwidth.** Each cohort was measured at one bandwidth.
